html:
The Kosovo declaration of independence was adopted by the assembly in Pristina on 17 February 2008, making Kosovo a state separate from Serbia.

Kosovo had been under United Nations rule since the Kosovo War of 1999. Talks on its status failed, and the declaration followed a plan for supervised independence drawn up by the UN envoy Martti Ahtisaari. The United States and most of the European Union recognised the new state, but Serbia, Russia, China and several EU members did not. The International Court of Justice found in 2010 that the declaration had not broken international law. Kosovo is not a UN member, and its north, mostly Serb, remains a source of tension.
sum: The Kosovo declaration of independence was adopted by the assembly in Pristina on 17 February 2008, making Kosovo a state separate from Serbia.
